labels.note: Differs only when the joined url ends with './', which needs odd segments like 'b.//'.
A '/' segment is no longer filtered, so resolveURL('/foo','/') yields '/foo//'.
With no inputs, base goes through parse/stringify; changes only when that isn't a round trip.
Same as the if(false) mutant: base is re-stringified instead of returned as-is.
A query-only segment gets an empty pathname appended, adding a stray '/' to the path.
A hash in an input segment no longer overrides the base hash.
An empty segment search can re-stringify or clear the base query; only edge-case differences.
Condition is always true, so it is the same as the if(true) mutant; edge-case query normalization.
